title: Billing adjustment workflow and metering ambiguity resolution
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: As Redwood expands enterprise contracts and runs pricing/packaging experiments, we see recurring edge cases where invoice adjustments are required but our current workflows are slow, error-prone, and inconsistent. Typical triggers: mid-cycle reserved capacity changes, overlapping burst credits, ambiguous metering (token vs. embedding units), and security-questionnaire discoveries that require migration to Private deployments. This ticket defines a formal billing adjustment workflow, rules for automatic vs. manual credits/refunds, and a metering ambiguity resolution process to reduce manual finance & CS work and close disputes faster.

Goals:
1) Reduce average time-to-resolution for invoice disputes from ~6 business days to <= 48 hours for standard cases.
2) Automate ~65% of straightforward proration and overage-credit calculations.
3) Provide a deterministic, auditable formula set and telemetry so Finance/Legal can accept adjustments for contract terms and security-driven migrations.

Scope:
- Define deterministic proration formulas for reserved capacity upgrades/downgrades, with rounding and cap rules.
- Create a metering ambiguity detector that flags invoices where metering surfaces (token vs embedding vs request unit) differ from the contract definition.
- Build an automated credit engine for low-risk adjustments and a clear escalation path for manual review.
- Update security questionnaire playbook to include billing ramifications (e.g., migration credits for Private deployment requests triggered by questionnaire answers).
- Add audit records to invoices and expose an internal UI for Finance/CS to approve or override automated credits.
acceptance_criteria: Automated credit engine applies correct proration for reserve changes in >=65% of test cases with known inputs and edge scenarios
Metering ambiguity detector flags >=95% of sampled mismatches between billed unit type and contract unit type in historical invoices
Internal billing UI shows full audit trail for each adjustment and allows Finance to approve/override with a single click
All credits/refunds produce GL-friendly ledger entries and a reconciliation report used by Finance (CSV export)
SLA: standard invoice disputes (clear-cut proration/overage errors) are resolved automatically or routed with recommended action within 48 hours
Security questionnaire escalations that require migration credits have a documented eligibility checklist and sample calculations
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (backend): implement proration formulas in billing-service with unit tests and historical backfill script
Phase 2 (detection): build metering ambiguity ruleset and run as nightly job across last 6 months of invoices to calibrate thresholds
Phase 3 (automation): credit-engine microservice issues provisional credits (pending Finance approval) and writes audit records to invoice history
Phase 4 (UI): add 'Adjustments' tab in internal Billing Console for Finance/CS with filters, approval workflow, and CSV export
Phase 5 (policy): collaborate with Legal/Revenue to finalize consumer-facing language and create template emails for customers
Coordinate with Accounting to ensure credits map to correct GL accounts and do not break revenue recognition reports
example_scenarios: Scenario A - Mid-cycle downgrade of reserved capacity: Customer has $12,000/month committed capacity (30 days). On day 10 they downgrade to half capacity. Proration credit = committed_fee * (unused_days/total_days) * capacity_reduction_percentage. Example: $12,000 * (20/30) * 0.5 = $4,000 credit applied to next invoice (round to nearest cent).

Scenario B - Overlapping burst credits: Customer used burst capacity for 3 days and consumed billed tokens that would have been covered by reserved buckets after a fixed lookback. We apply burst-first billing then reserved usage; where double-billing identified, auto-credit lesser-of(consumed_cost, reserved_unused_value). Implementation must avoid negative invoices.

Scenario C - Metering ambiguity (embedding mislabeled): Contract measures 'embedding units' but invoice shows 'tokens' due to model change. Detector flags mismatch; automatic remediation path attempts to map tokens->embedding using model-specific conversion factor and offers provisional credit while awaiting manual approval if conversion variance >10%.

Scenario D - Security questionnaire triggers migration to Private: Customer requires on-prem in security questionnaire; Finance policy offers a one-time migration credit equal to 25% of remaining committed reserved capacity fee for the month the migration occurs. Eligibility checklist and manual signoff required.
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: Backend proration library merged behind feature flag; run against historical invoices to verify outputs
Week 3: Deploy metering ambiguity detector to staging and tune thresholds; present findings to Finance and Legal
Week 4: Launch credit-engine in canary for internal test customers and Finance team; add UI approvals
Week 5: Pilot with 3 enterprise customers via CS; collect feedback and adjust wording in notifications
Week 6: Full rollout behind a runtime flag; monitor key metrics and enable default after 2 weeks of stable behaviour
Post-release: Add automated reconciliation job and include changes in monthly billing runbook
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Automated credits map incorrectly to GL accounts causing accounting reconciliation issues. Mitigation: Parallel dry-run ledger exports and review by Finance before live writes.
Risk: Metering detector false positives create unnecessary CS noise. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and provisional credit state pending human approval.
Risk: Security questionnaire migrations abused for free credits. Mitigation: eligibility checklist, legal signoff, and cap on cumulative migration credits per contract year.
Risk: Edge-case rounding differences across currencies. Mitigation: canonical rounding rules per currency and sample outputs for major currencies in spec.
notes: 2025-02-13: Kickoff meeting with Finance, Legal, and Eng billing squad. Agreed to prioritize deterministic proration rules.
2025-02-18: Eng-squad implemented initial proration library and unit tests (PR 847).
2025-02-26: Ran ambiguity detector across last 6 months; identified 112 invoices with potential unit mismatches (~0.8% of total).
2025-03-03: Finance reviewed sample GL mappings; requested CSV export for month-end close verification.
2025-03-04: Updated ticket with UI requirements and set target pilot customers (3 enterprise accounts).
